What does this tell us?** 5. **What percentage of variance is shared between the variables?** % 6. **A possible third variable could be:** ::: --- ## Key Reminders for the Exam ### Design Types | Design | Key Feature | Test | |--------|-------------|------| | Between-subjects | Different participants in each condition | Independent t-test | | Within-subjects | Same participants in all conditions | Paired t-test | | Matched pairs | Participants paired, one per condition | Paired t-test | | Correlational | Measuring relationship, no manipulation | Pearson's r | ### Effect Size Guidelines (Cohen's d) - **0.2** = Small - **0.5** = Medium - **0.8** = Large ### Important Distinctions - p < .05 = significant at α = .05 - p > .05 = not significant at α = .05 - Correlation ≠ causation - No IV in correlational designs --- ## Summary Checklist Before the exam, verify you can: - [ ] Quickly identify design types from descriptions - [ ] Identify IV and DV (or recognise no IV in correlational designs) - [ ] Match designs to appropriate tests - [ ] Write one-tailed and two-tailed hypotheses - [ ] Interpret p-values (significant vs not significant) - [ ] Interpret effect sizes (small, medium, large) - [ ] Explain why correlation ≠ causation - [ ] Recognise matched pairs designs ::: {.callout-important} ## MCQ Exam This Week The exam is during Wednesday's lecture time. Bring a pen. You will have the full 2-hour slot. Good luck! :::
